crises.title: Economic Collapse
crises.description: Businesses are failing, unemployment is soaring, and basic goods are becoming scarce. The district's economy has hit rock bottom.

advisors.economist: Tighten the belt. Pain now prevents total ruin later.
advisors.ranger: Cuts to green programs will scar the land deeper.
advisors.monk: Shared suffering can build compassion, or break it.

advisors.economist: Stimulus puts coins in empty pockets.
advisors.ranger: Bulldozers for jobs still fell ancient trees.
advisors.monk: Work that unites hands can heal hearts.

crises.title: Cultural Erosion
crises.description: Traditional practices are being forgotten, languages are disappearing, and the youth are abandoning ancestral values.

advisors.economist: Classroom hours cost productive labor.
advisors.ranger: Names of plants and animals live in old words.
advisors.monk: Wisdom must be planted young to grow deep.

advisors.economist: Subsidies drain the treasury.
advisors.ranger: Natural dyes and woven reeds honor the earth.
advisors.monk: The hand that crafts with devotion holds the past.

crises.title: Governance Crisis
crises.description: The local administration is paralyzed by corruption, inefficiency, and a lack of public confidence.

advisors.economist: Purge creates vacancies and uncertainty.
advisors.ranger: A clean stream runs clear after the flood.
advisors.monk: Cutting the rotten branch saves the tree.

advisors.economist: Local markets know local needs.
advisors.ranger: Villages protect their own forests best.
advisors.monk: Trust given to many hands builds a stronger roof.

crises.title: Rising Social Unrest
crises.description: Protests are turning violent, and the streets are filled with anger. The people demand change, but chaos is spreading.

advisors.economist: Dialogue is cheaper than broken windows.
advisors.ranger: Peaceful valleys allow seeds to grow.
advisors.monk: Listening is the first step to understanding.

advisors.economist: Order must exist before profit.
advisors.ranger: Violence shatters the harmony of the wild.
advisors.monk: A fist cannot grasp the truth.

crises.title: Environmental Catastrophe
crises.description: Deforestation, pollution, and climate change have pushed the ecosystem to the brink. Floods and droughts are becoming frequent.

advisors.economist: Regulation strangles enterprise.
advisors.ranger: Finally, the forest gets a shield.
advisors.monk: Protecting life is the highest duty.

options.text: Invest in green technology and reforestation

advisors.economist: Green jobs are still jobs.
advisors.ranger: Planting a tree is planting hope.
advisors.monk: Healing the earth heals the mind.

crises.title: Corruption Scandal Erupts
crises.description: A massive corruption ring has been exposed, implicating officials and business leaders. Trust in institutions is shattered.

advisors.economist: Trials freeze investment.
advisors.ranger: Justice, like rain, clears the air.
advisors.monk: Karma must be met, not hidden.

advisors.economist: Stability returns faster with forgiveness.
advisors.ranger: A wound half-healed still festers.
advisors.monk: Mercy opens the door to change.

crises.title: Crisis of Public Trust
crises.description: The public has lost all confidence in the government and institutions. Civic participation is at an all-time low.

options.text: Launch transparency and citizen engagement campaign

advisors.economist: Campaigns cost money with no direct return.
advisors.ranger: Open skies hide no storms.
advisors.monk: Truth spoken plainly rebuilds the bridge.

advisors.economist: Bureaucracy breeds more bureaucracy.
advisors.ranger: Watchers in the tower spot the smoke early.
advisors.monk: External eyes see what internal ones miss.

crises.title: Foreign Influence Overreach
crises.description: External powers are exerting excessive control over the district's politics and economy, threatening sovereignty.

advisors.economist: Renegotiation risks trade retaliation.
advisors.ranger: A bird in its own nest sings freely.
advisors.monk: Independence is the root of self-respect.

advisors.economist: Seized assets still need skilled hands.
advisors.ranger: What was taken once is taken again.
advisors.monk: Grasping creates more grasping.

crises.title: Ecological Collapse
crises.description: The environment is severely degraded, and natural disasters are devastating communities. The situation is dire.

advisors.economist: Moving people is cheaper than moving mountains.
advisors.ranger: Abandoning the land abandons its spirit.
advisors.monk: Even impermanence deserves a dignified farewell.

advisors.economist: Restoration is an investment in future harvests.
advisors.ranger: The forest remembers those who return to mend it.
advisors.monk: Healing what was broken is the deepest practice.

crises.title: Civil Unrest Amidst Distrust
crises.description: Angry citizens distrust authorities, and protests are escalating into civil disobedience.

advisors.economist: Talking does not fill empty stomachs.
advisors.ranger: A circle of voices is stronger than a wall.
advisors.monk: Reconciliation is built one conversation at a time.

advisors.economist: Security spending is a necessary drain.
advisors.ranger: Cages do not tame the wild, they only hide it.
advisors.monk: Fear is a poor foundation for peace.

crises.title: Economic Vulnerability to Foreign Influence
crises.description: The weak economy is easily manipulated by foreign interests, leading to exploitation and loss of control.

options.text: Impose capital controls and trade barriers

advisors.economist: Walls around money starve the market.
advisors.ranger: A closed valley keeps its water, but also its floods.
advisors.monk: Attachment to control often breeds chaos.

advisors.economist: Many ropes are harder to cut than one.
advisors.ranger: A forest with many species weathers the storm.
advisors.monk: Balance comes from many supports, not one.

crises.title: Cultural and Governance Decline
crises.description: Both cultural identity and administrative competence are rapidly deteriorating. The fabric of society is unraveling.

advisors.economist: Reform is expensive and slow.
advisors.ranger: Roots deepened hold the soil against any wind.
advisors.monk: Renewing tradition and discipline is the middle way.

options.text: Merge with neighboring district for stability

advisors.economist: Consolidation reduces overhead.
advisors.ranger: Two rivers merged lose their separate songs.
advisors.monk: Surrendering identity for comfort is no peace.

crises.title: Identity Crisis: Trust and Culture Eroding
crises.description: With public trust crumbling and cultural pride fading, society is losing its sense of shared purpose. Urgent action is needed.

options.text: Launch a 'Pride in Our Roots' festival and civic education

advisors.economist: Festivals generate tourism and local spending.
advisors.ranger: Celebration of place reminds people why it matters.
advisors.monk: Joy in heritage is a light against darkness.

options.text: Create community councils with real decision-making power

advisors.economist: Decentralization speeds some decisions, slows others.
advisors.ranger: Those who live in the forest should guide its care.
advisors.monk: Power shared is power multiplied.

crises.title: Resource Scarcity and Economic Decline
crises.description: Over‑exploitation of natural resources has depleted forests and rivers, crippling both the economy and the ecosystem.

options.text: Introduce sustainable resource quotas and invest in eco‑industry

advisors.economist: Quotas hurt short-term output but build long-term stock.
advisors.ranger: Taking only what returns is the law of the wild.
advisors.monk: Restraint today is abundance tomorrow.

options.text: Open resource extraction to foreign companies for quick revenue

advisors.economist: Quick revenue plugs the leak today.
advisors.ranger: Selling the mountain leaves only a hole.
advisors.monk: Desperation is the mother of regret.
